Thanks — technical note with the recommended pattern below.

Short-lived service-account approach (recommended):
- Create an IAM role (arn:aws:iam::XXXXX:role/restricted-vendr-upload) with a trust policy allowing our STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or AssumeRole from a service account we control.
- Minimize scope: allow s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging to the evidence-prefix only (e.g. arn:aws:s3:::redwood-evidence/brightleaf/*). Block ACL and public-read.
- Presign policy: TTL = 24h, max content-length 30MB, enforce Content-MD5 header on upload and require x-amz-meta-steward:brightleaf-steward-attestation header so we can link the object to the attestation.
- Rotation: we’ll set an automated job to revoke the role immediately after the window and rotate any temporary keys.

Operational steps I can implement if you want me to:
1) Create role + policy in the Redwood acct and produce a one-time presign URL generator endpoint (HTTPS) that Brightleaf can call with an upload manifest.
2) Post the presign URL and expiry to Jenna via an encrypted channel (we use DocuSign attestation link + direct email).

Attached is a sample presign policy JSON and a stub we use internally. If Brightleaf prefers an upload via Vendr API instead of S3 presign, call that out and we’ll issue a time-limited API token with the same constraints.

- Karthik

Attachments: s3-presign-policy.json
